**Publius Helvius Pertinax **was Roman emperor for the first three months of 193, succeeding Commodus and becoming the first ruler of the turbulent Year of the Five Emperors. 
The son of a [freedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Roman_freedmen), Pertinax rose from modest origins through a military career. He distinguished himself in the [Roman–Parthian War of 161–166](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman%E2%80%93Parthian_War_of_161%E2%80%93166) and went on to hold a succession of governorships and senior commands. He also sat in the [Roman Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Senate), where he was a contemporary of the historian [<u>Cassius Dio</u>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassius_Dio).
Cassius Dio, who knew him personally, called him "an excellent and upright man" who governed with integrity and frugality.[25] He criticised only the haste of his reforms, which provoked resentment and led to his downfall.[26]
Later writers echoed this assessment. [Niccolò Machiavelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niccol%C3%B2_Machiavelli) cited him in [*The Prince*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Prince) as a good ruler fatally undermined by trying to reform corrupt soldiers too quickly. [David Hume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hume) praised him as an "excellent prince". In 1788, at the Virginia Ratifying Convention, [John Dawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Dawson_(Virginia_politician)) referred to Pertinax’s murder as a warning against standing armies.[27]
The French journalist [André Géraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9_G%C3%A9raud) (1882–1974) wrote under the pseudonym “Pertinax”.
In the alternate history novel [*Romanitas*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanitas_(novel)) by [Sophia McDougall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophia_McDougall), Pertinax survives the coup and enacts reforms that preserve the Roman Empire into the modern age.
The UK's oldest [gorilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_lowland_gorilla), Pertinax who died aged 42 at [Paignton Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paignton_Zoo) in Devon, was named after the emperor.
